LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING – LETTERS OF APPLICATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we make applications whenever we need formal opportunities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise the components of a letter of application for information
2. write a letter of application for a scholarship for effective communication

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing – Letters of Application makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner contributes to group decision-making when identifying the components of a well-written scholarship application letter.
2. Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner uses digital technology to search online and offline for samples of scholarship application letters. 54 Values:
3. Integrity: It is developed as the learner displays transparency by sharing their written letters with peers for review.
4. Composing and performing songs during interclass festivals in school
5. Summaries of read texts

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we make applications whenever we need formal opportunities?
2. How do application letters differ from other letters?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
